answer.why_different: The generator could not infer a concrete producer-hosted server address for the notification endpoint. It replaced the official server-variable URL template with an empty URL, removed the associated variable definition, and added explanatory metadata describing that uncertainty; this is primarily a different address and partly a different metadata structure.
answer.spec_3gpp: The provided 3GPP evidence defines the notification resource and its path as `/notificationSink`, but does not establish a host URL. It therefore does not justify replacing the official consumer-side server template with an empty URL.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI requires a Server Object `url`, which is the URL to the target host and supports server-variable substitution. Specification extensions are allowed, so the added `x-openapi-gen-note` is structurally valid, but it does not compensate for losing the usable server address.
answer.clearer_why: The official document provides a usable URL template and explains that the server is on the consumer side. The generated document explains its uncertainty, but an empty server URL is less useful to API readers and clients.

The description is an allowed Server Object field, but the supplied 3GPP evidence only specifies the `/notificationSink` resource and does not establish that the server cannot be determined. The usefulness and correctness of this added explanation are therefore not decided by the evidence; see S2 and O10.

evidence.text: ### Specification Extensions While the OpenAPI Specification tries to accommodate most use cases, additional data can be added to extend the specification at certain points. The extensions properties are implemented as patterned fields that are always prefixed by `"x-"`. Field Pattern | Type | Description ---|:---:|--- ^x- | Any | Allows extensions to the OpenAPI Schema. The field name MUST begin with `x-`, for example, `x-internal-id`. The value can be `null`, a primitive, an array or an object. Can have any valid JSON format value. The extensions may or may not be supported by the available tooling, but those may be extended as well to add requested support (if tools are internal or open-sourced).
